81014.subject: 🚔 Claude sent the police a fake murder tip
81014.body:
----------
######           [Subscribe](https://academynews.genai.works/)   -    [Collaborate with us](https://utm.genai.works/r/cq9vsh4)


--------------------
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/8776fa6e-e2d0-4aec-9648-1bed6de3a659/GenAI_Daily_Banner.jpg?t=1778687445)
Caption: 


----------

----------
**Welcome back!** It's recap day, with this week's five biggest stories and five tools to try this weekend. Claude sent police a fake murder tip, and an OpenAI engineer allegedly bugged his own bosses. Anthropic also warned AI could hide on your cheap gadgets, and one developer cloned Microsoft Office with Claude.

**In today's Generative AI Newsletter:**

* **Claude:** Why did Claude lie to the police?

* **OpenAI:** What was hiding in the toilet paper behind OpenAI's TV?

* **Anthropic:** Could your cheap smart gadgets end up hosting a rogue AI?

* **Coding:** Why did Claude force Anthropic to ditch git?

* **Microsoft:** Do you still need to pay for Office?


----------







----------
## Claude sent the police a fake murder tip

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/1d226dde-dd54-419e-9375-41322bbd7ca3/09fdf7be-88bc-4c8d-8aba-b04442c55ed5.jpg?t=1791796098)
Caption: 

During a test, Claude [sent Philadelphia police a tip](https://www.anthropic.com/research/investigating-unintended-model-actions) about an unsolved murder. It said it remembered seeing someone matching the description near the scene, and it made the whole thing up.

By Wednesday, the FTC had [subpoenaed OpenAI and Anthropic](https://www.axios.com/2026/10/15/ftc-openai-anthropic-ai-safety-investigation) for their records on AI going rogue, with more than 50 pages of demands each.

A source told Axios the agency plans to make top executives at both companies testify. We’ll be the first to update you on how that goes.


----------







----------
## An OpenAI engineer used ChatGPT to bug his bosses

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/cef7d44f-f894-4432-910c-f5dac2658a20/dbaad53b-2ccb-463f-9d56-ca2aa781605e.jpg?t=1792051113)
Caption: 

Prosecutors say an OpenAI engineer [used ChatGPT to plan a hidden recorder](https://www.justice.gov/usao-ndca/pr/saudi-national-arrested-installing-surreptitious-audio-recording-device-openai-san), then hid it behind the TV in an executive meeting room, wrapped in toilet paper.

OpenAI's security team found it and set up its own camera, which caught him checking behind the TV.

He was fired and arrested on Oct 9. Prosecutors say he'd booked one-way tickets to Saudi Arabia for himself and his family, and they haven't said who, if anyone, he was working for.

We expect it’s the first of many espionage cases. AI CEOs
